reviews.title: Keeps losing connection to TV
reviews.text:
The ThinQ app previously maintained a stable connection to my LG TV, but recent updates appear to have introduced issues with network persistence. My TV now disconnects intermittently, and the ThinQ app reports the device as offline even though the TV remains connected to the local network.

Based on testing, the problem seems related to how ThinQ handles WiFi band transitions. My router uses Smart WiFi, which automatically steers devices between 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands. When the TV is moved between bands, ThinQ appears to lose its cloud session or fails to re-establish the connection reliably. The app will occasionally reconnect, but the session drops again as soon as the band changes.

All local network settings, LG account settings, and TV configurations have been verified and are correct. However, because I rely on Smart WiFi for other devices, disabling band steering is not an option. ThinQ currently does not seem robust enough to maintain a persistent connection in environments where the router dynamically manages WiFi bands.

Improved handling of band steering or more resilient reconnection logic would significantly help users whose routers automatically optimise WiFi channels and bands.

reviews.title: App Updated now both TVs gone
reviews.text: I had been using the LG ThinQ app for a while to control both of the LG TVs in my household just fine. It was a great experience with a good and reliable connection as a TV remote. The latest update however has lost both of my TVs on the app, and it can’t find them again when trying to re-add them back. This needs fixed as soon as possible, otherwise the app is pointless and I’ll end up looking for another TV brand with a proper functioning app remote.

I just wanted a simple remote for my LG TV. Instead, ThinQ forces me to keep GPS location turned on at all times or the remote features don’t work. Why the hell does a TV remote need my real-time location? Are you tracking me while I sit on my couch?

reviews.title: The actual TV remote feature is buried somewhere in here
reviews.text:
Sadly, the one feature I really want – the LG TV remote on my phone – is buried under a sea of things I have absolutely no interest in whatsoever, but which the app does not allow me to hide or re-order so that the features I want are at the top of the oafe.  TV Show recommendations, Apps, and a “Share” feature… I have to scroll past these before I even get to the device inputs. 

The remote control screen is a temporary overlay screen, that is missing a simple directional control (up/down/left/right) to navigate the various TV menus.

And if you navigate to another app and come back, you have to relaunch that overlay screen every single time.

It’s a terrible UI design, and I wonder how many people genuinely use the other 95% of what the app does, which seems to be purposefully positioned to get in the way of anyone who merely wants to control their TV from their phone with no other distractions.

reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text:
The new tv tells you to download the app to setup the tv rather than having to use the remote - great! The app collections your information, asks for new account creation yada yada - still probably worth it for the eventual features and ease of setting up.

Then it asks you to turn on location, track you, enable cookies. Apparently all important. Finally - can’t find the TV without it being connected to the internet. Can’t setup the tv, including the internet, without going through setup. 

What a waste of time. Unless you’re setting up a tv you’ve already set up (I say sarcastically). Either way, LG has my information and my time has been wasted.

Update: to set up the WiFi you need to connect to your mobile hotspot, disable IPV6, update the software and then turn the power off and on. Then you have a TV that blasts adverts at you, has no ability to change inputs without using voice control, resets the apps list to push LG channels and constantly has issues with telling you to set your region to access content when your region is already set. Apparently these have been problems for years, LG doesn’t care - they just push adverts and AI because ignoring your actual customers is definitely a good strategic move.

reviews.title: Intrusive
reviews.text:
Let me save LG the trouble of posting the same canned response again: saying Precise Location is “only used to search for networks” or “check power status on the local network” does not justify requiring it for a washer.

Discovering a device on my home Wi-Fi is not the same as needing my exact physical location. That response explains LG’s implementation choice, not why customers should tolerate it. If the app was designed so invasive permissions are mandatory for basic setup, that is LG’s design failure.

The privacy policy is overreaching, the permission request is excessive, and the scripted replies are not reassuring. They just confirm that LG thinks this is acceptable.

It is not. I am returning the washer over this.

Edit: Adding to address LG’s Inane response:

LG’s response is a perfect example of the problem. I did not complain because I “dislike terms and conditions.” I complained because the app demands excessive permissions and hides behind broad legal language for a washing machine.

Their reply completely sidesteps the real issue. They still have not explained why a washer being added over Wi-Fi should require anything beyond reasonable local network access, nor why customers should accept invasive design choices just because LG made them “required.”

A canned corporate apology is not an answer. It just confirms that LG would rather deflect than justify the overreach. I am have already returned the washer over this.

reviews.title: To use the word “smart” is marketing hype
reviews.text:
The functionality for my fridge freezer is rather limited but probably adequate for most people. 
I would like to see the ability to boost freezer, and maybe fridge, on a user schedule to allow best use of off-peak cheap tariffs.

Edit after a couple of years: whenever there is a power cut my “smart” fridge fails to reconnect to the network. This isn’t really a big problem as the “smart” functionality doesn’t really exist. Being able to monitor the fridge’s status or change it isn’t really smart, it’s a remote control. I now know of someone that uses Home Assistant to change temperature settings to take advantage of his tariff variability. I don’t need such fancy control but I still don’t even get a timer.
